rationale: Start with a broad gradient to observe all 21 compounds and locate the elution window and critical pairs. This moderate gradient duration provides a useful resolution baseline without an unnecessarily long run.

Change only gradient duration to identify which critical pairs respond to a shallower slope, particularly the nearly coeluting late triplet. The comparison will guide subsequent window trimming and temperature adjustments.

Test temperature selectivity against injection 1 while restoring its faster gradient. Higher temperature may separate the slope-insensitive middle pair and late triplet while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

Complete a temperature-selectivity comparison at the same gradient. Cooling may improve the early cluster that worsened at 60 C and reveal whether the late triplet separates on the opposite side of its temperature-dependent crossing.

Use a higher starting organic fraction to make room for a shallower gradient within the 10-minute elution target. This tests whether slope and window changes can separate the remaining critical pairs at the most promising temperature.

Retain the low starting organic fraction to protect early-pair resolution while making the gradient shallower than injection 3. This should test gains in the late triplet with the last peak still near the 10-minute target.

Combine an intermediate starting fraction with a shallower slope to improve the late triplet while preserving more early separation than injection 5. The last peak should remain close to, but below, 10 minutes.

Explore a higher starting fraction with a shallower gradient to improve the late triplet and middle pair. Early peaks remain a risk, but the observed order changes suggest a potentially better-separated window beyond phi0 0.15.

Test a modest temperature reduction at the best gradient to move the early critical pair away from its apparent crossing. This isolates whether improved early selectivity outweighs any loss in late-triplet resolution.

Test whether moving beyond the early-pair crossing and further flattening the gradient improves total resolution. The higher starting fraction should offset the longer gradient, though compression of the first three peaks is the main risk.

Refine injection 5 with a slightly shallower gradient, using its remaining time margin to improve the middle pair and late triplet. Starting at 0.15 avoids the severe early-pair crossing seen at 0.20.

Test temperature selectivity in the 0.15 starting window, where cooling may improve both the first pair and the early triplet. Injection 5 has enough time margin to accommodate this temperature reduction.

Slightly flatten the best method’s slope to spend its remaining time margin on the critical pairs. The final fraction remains above the estimated last-peak elution fraction, so all peaks should elute during the gradient near 10 minutes.
Fine-tune the low-starting-fraction alternative with a slope just shallower than injection 6. This should improve its three deficient pairs while placing the final peak very close to 10 minutes.

Explore a faster gradient followed by a moderate-organic hold as a different selectivity regime. The hold may spread the late cluster differently from a continuous gradient while the low starting fraction protects early retention.

Move the late triplet into the final hold to test selectivity at a fixed organic fraction rather than during the gradient. This faster ramp leaves time for hold-phase separation, although early-pair compression may limit the score.
Return to the promising 0.15 window and test a small temperature adjustment. Cooling by 5 C may improve the first pair and balance the early triplet while keeping the final peak below 10 minutes.
Test one shallower step beyond injection 11 to measure whether improved late-triplet resolution can outweigh a small time penalty. This brackets the optimum slope in the 0.15 starting window.
Bracket the best method with the next shallower accessible slope. This will determine whether additional late-triplet separation compensates for moving the last peak slightly beyond 10 minutes.

Test a distinct, hold-dominated separation by reaching 0.50 organic quickly. This places the late cluster well into the hold, where its selectivity may differ substantially from the gradients already tested.

Test the cooler selectivity regime in the 0.20 starting window, where the early critical pair may move beyond its crossing. Shortening the gradient offsets increased retention and should keep the last peak near 10 minutes.

Test whether moderate cooling repairs the early and middle-pair losses in the 0.25 starting window. A shorter gradient than injection 10 compensates for increased retention and preserves the chance of finishing within 10 minutes.

Use injection 22’s remaining time margin to flatten the slope slightly and improve its deficient middle pair and late triplet. The final peak is expected near 10 minutes, with the endpoint still comfortably above its elution fraction.

Refine injection 23 with a slightly higher temperature and shallower slope to improve the late critical pair while targeting a last peak below 10 minutes. This tests whether those gains outweigh modest losses in early selectivity.

Make a final local refinement around injection 23: modest cooling may improve the early critical cluster, while a slightly steeper slope offsets the retention increase. This tests whether those gains outweigh reduced late-triplet resolution, with the last peak targeted near 10 minutes.
